summary: Linguist Louis Léon Duvau studied at the University of Paris, Leipzig, and Rome, learning under Michel Bréal and Ferdinand de Saussure. He held posts at Burgundy, Lille, the École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Collège de France.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, Theodor Bloch, and Alfred Foucher, earning a PhD from Paris. He held professorships at Lyon, the Sorbonne, and Paris, and a post at the EPHE.

Linguist Louis Trolle Hjelmslev earned an M.A. at the University of Copenhagen and studied under Holger Pedersen, Antoine Meillet, and Joseph Vendryes. He held posts at Aarhus University (1934–1937) and Copenhagen as professor of Sammenlignende Sprogvidenskab from 1937.

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies educated at Liège, Leuven, Sorbonne, and Leiden under Lévi, Kern, and others. He served as professor at Ghent University from 1893 to 1929.
Linguist and Indologist Louis-François Meunier studied under Eugène Burnouf and Michel Bréal.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology, studying at the Collège de France. He was conservator at the Bibliothèque nationale and administrator and professor of Persian at INALCO and the Collège de France.

Louise Allison Cort is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology who studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College. She served as curator of ceramics at the Freer and Sackler Galleries of the Smithsonian Institution from circa 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, studied under traditional teacher Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at Leeds.

Louise Roche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held a post at the University of Munich in 2023 and is attested as an assistant at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Gauhati University under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma and studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch is an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and studied under Th. P. van Baaren, J. H. Hospers, F. Leemhuis, and A. S. van der Woude.
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Lozang Trinlae, a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies scholar, studied at Northeastern, Harvard, and Claremont School of Theology (PhD 2017). She was CEO of Educational Visions and Methods and visiting lecturer at the University of Tartu.

Lubor Hájek was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his PhD at Charles University under Otakar Pertold and Vincenc Lesný. He served as director of Oriental Collections at the National Gallery Prague from 1952 to 1986.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from circa 1978 to 1983 and held a post there beginning circa 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa works in linguistics, Indology, and computational fields, holding posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned a doctorate at the Free University of Berlin. He served as director at IsIAO and was associate professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2020–2021).
Luchun Wu is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar affiliated with Ghent University, where she held a post in 2025 and is attested as a PhD researcher in 2026.

Lucia Catherine Graeme Grieve was an Indologist who studied at Wellesley College, Oxford, and Columbia University (PhD 1898). She taught at Staunton, Frederick, Freehold, Mississippi Synodical College, and Young's Female College.
